result.title: Structured Visual Landscape: Generating Preferred Representations in Biological and Artificial Neural Networks
result.summary: Understanding how neurons respond to visual stimulus is an important question in both deep learning and neuroscience. It has significant implications for enhancing the interpretability of black-box artificial neural networks and for understanding the visual representation in the human brain. We propose a structured visual representations landscape and design an activation-based prior that allows us to effectively regularize the landscape with activations from brain regions or neural network units. Our model Vis-Lens integrates a variational autoencoder and a diffusion model into an image generation framework. It enables the generation of natural, realistic preferred images by directly modifying the activation-regularized latent codes without per-image iterative optimization. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework on both artificial neural networks and human visual cortex using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data. Our framework improves activation modulation and image realism compared with a recent state-of-the-art method for generating preferred visual representations of these neural targets.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出“结构化视觉表征景观”与基于激活的先验，结合 VAE 与扩散模型构建 Vis-Lens 框架，在无需逐图迭代优化的情况下，通过直接修改激活正则化的 latent code 生成自然逼真的“偏好图像”，并在人工神经网络与 fMRI 人脑视觉皮层数据上验证其优于近期同类方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用激活约束反转内部表征、生成能解释神经单元偏好的图像，可能可供核查作为探测 VLM 内部状态是否保留具体视觉细节的读出手段；但该工作目标是刺激图像生成与可解释性，而非推理状态生成或使用。
